name: 101 Main (The Bella)
headline: The NHP Foundation is building The Bella, 52 new studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI on Frisco's Main Street, with 2025 Round One federal 9% and state credits from CHFA. It is Frisco's first LIHTC development.
why_it_matters: It shows how a small resort town can make a 9% deal work: the Town upzoned the site through its affordable housing incentive program, put in local gap money and land, and set up its own housing authority for a property tax exemption, with Prop 123 land banking money behind the site. Financing closed and demolition began in late August 2026.

status.label: Financing closed; demolition began August 2026
status.detail: NHPF announced the financial closing on 2026-08-27, and Summit Daily reported demolition of the old office building began that week. Completion is expected in November 2027 (late 2027 per Summit Daily). There is no public building permit record in hand, and vertical construction has not yet been reported.

next_step: Watch for the Town of Frisco building permit and the start of vertical construction after demolition, which Summit Daily said would take three to four weeks from 2026-08-26.

background.text: NHPF announced in January 2024 that it planned 45 to 50 workforce units at 101 W Main, a 1970s office site with what it called a long development history, and that it would seek LIHTC and Prop 123 funding.

In May 2023 the Frisco Town Council approved Ordinance 23-14 on two NHPF projects (101 West Main and 602 Galena), including a $2.5M Town loan for NHPF to buy 101 West Main. At that time the plan for 101 West Main was 4% credits with tax-exempt bonds; it later won 9% credits instead.

In February 2024 Summit Daily reported NHPF owned the site and had applied to rezone it from mixed-use to a Planned Unit Development. The Town's Affordable Housing Development Incentive Program let density rise from about 11 market-rate units to 52 and cut parking, with on-street overnight parking and car sharing.
The 2025 application notes changes since a 2024 application, so the deal applied unsuccessfully in the 2024 round (inferred from the narrative).

The Town and NHPF signed a Second Amended and Restated Development Agreement on 2024-06-25 and a 99-year ground lease on 2025-08-27. Council approved Ordinance 26-16, amending and restating the ground lease for the LIHTC closing, on second reading on 2026-06-09.

On 2026-07-14 Council approved Ordinance 26-12 on second reading, and the Frisco Community Housing Development Authority approved documents subordinating the Town's loans to the two outside lenders and transferring rights to West Main Apartments, LLLP.
The application promised a 99-year affordability covenant with the Town. The 99-year ground lease is for long-term affordable housing.

The Town says its housing fund is strained by commitments including 101 W. Main (52 units, $6.4M) and 602 Galena (54 units, $8.1M), and in June 2026 it approved selling four Mary Ruth Place units to offset that.
The narrative says rents are 18% to 79% below market, cites a 1.8% comparable vacancy rate and notes that The Larkspur in Breckenridge drew over 770 applications in four days.
Demolition started late because cell tower equipment on the old building had to be relocated first.
NHPF's other Frisco project, The Scout, is a few blocks away and is opening in September 2026, per NHPF.

discrepancies.text: CHFA, the application and the Town give the income mix as 30%, 50% and 80% AMI, while NHPF's closing release says 30%, 60% and 80% AMI with a 60% average.

The Town's support is given as more than $14.6M in cash flow loans in the 2025 application, a $6.4M contribution in the Town's June 2026 recap, and about $4.9M of soft financing in NHPF's closing release.

The application, the Town's housing inventory page and Summit Daily in 2024 say NHPF bought and owns the site, while the Town's June 2026 recap describes it as Town-owned land leased to NHPF for 99 years.
NHPF says demolition began on August 25, 2026, while Summit Daily says it began on Wednesday, August 26.

The 2025 application assumed R4 for tax credit equity and construction and permanent loans, while the closing release names U.S. Bank as construction lender and Cedar Rapids Bank & Trust as permanent lender.
A state official quoted in NHPF's closing release refers to 54 new housing options at The Bella, while every other source gives 52 units.
